title: Keep strict check's lost-requirements comparison when a branch turns SDD off
description: Keep strict check's lost-requirements comparison when a branch turns SDD off
acceptance_criteria: On a branch whose trusted comparison base has SDD enabled, `check --strict` refuses an unexplained loss of a canonical requirement and names it when the branch sets `enabled` to false or deletes `.specsync/sdd.json`, committed or not, as `change audit --strict` does. A project whose comparison base never enabled SDD, or has it disabled there, keeps drift-only strict check.

answers.constraints: Read the policy the way `change audit` already does, from the trusted comparison base, and bring nothing else of the lifecycle audit into `check` (REQ-cmd-check-004). Keep plain `check`, and a project whose comparison base never enabled SDD or has it disabled, on the drift-only path. Leave the selection, removal accounting and bounded reads of REQ-change-169 as they are.
